main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large snowy roof slope (rows 8-35) above a log-wall front with a door and two lit windows (rows 37-62)
top_band: Roof slope in white and pale blue-grey snow, rows ~8-35 with a bright snow lip at rows 32-35; it reads as a large, light, foreshortened surface seen from above
evidence: In a column through the middle, the roof snow runs from about row 8 to 35. It ends at a bright snow front edge with icicles, then a dark eave shadow at rows 37-39. Below that is the wall face (log planks, door, windows) down to row 62. The roof is a clear top surface with a distinct front face below it, matching the Beodeul house references. Windows have dark shutters and sills, and the door has a frame and iron bands, so the front reads as inset. No receding side faces.

style.evidence: The snow has 4-5 tones (white, pale blue, mid blue-grey, shadow blue) in clumped patches. The wood has several browns with grain and log ends, and the windows have warm gradient glow. Outlines are dark brown beside wood and blue-grey beside snow, not black. Icicles, the stone chimney and the bare branches add detail. Tile density is comparable to the references, with no large flat fills.
